additional_info.subject: ID0474745-DC/Si-D/CH-[Y2/T10 4002922671] Charging interruption CRM:03056000990
additional_info.body:
Dear Alexander,
Thank you for contacting our eMobility Support, I hope this email finds you well.
Following your request and after reviewing the logs, we can see that the issue is related to the session duration.
We can confirm that this behavior is linked to the
cooling system's thermal management
.
This means the charger was waiting for the cable temperature to stabilize before continuing the charging process at full capacity.
With best regards,
eMobility Technical Support Team – Felipe Moraes
Please do not change the subject line when replying to this email.

Hi Filipe
Please don't be angry with me, but I strongly doubt this analysis.
The charge is only 52 kW, and the outside temperature in Switzerland is currently around 0°C or even below freezing. With such a low power output and at these ambient temperatures, how can the temperature in the cable heat up so much that it takes more than 12 hours to resume charging?
That can't be right. Please involve your colleagues at L3.

additional_info.subject: ID0474745-DC/Si-D/CH-[Y2/T10 4002922671] Charging interruption CRM:03056000990
additional_info.body:
Hi Alex, good afternoon.
After the tests today, it's clear that the feedback of the SiD works based on voltage and not on the real feedback.
This means that the contactor really opened and it's not the feedback contact.
From my point of view, the component that is causing this sounds definitely to be StateMonitor KF14 as we have abortions from both outlets and not just 1.
I would start from replacing KF14.
I will forward this ticket to RC-CH queue.
Thanks!
Best regards,
Francisco

additional_info.subject: ID0474745-DC/Si-D/CH-[Y2/T10 4002922671] Charging interruption CRM:03056000990
additional_info.body:
I forgot to include.
The reason why the session is limited to 100A is due to the Error Flag about the Cooling Unit warning level
I talked with my colleagues and it's not recommend to turn on the pump since the readings are physical and not via communication cables.
We should check if the level is indeed low and fill it up again.
Thank you!
Best regards,
Francisco

additional_info.subject: 0474745 - ID0474745-DC/Si-D/CH-[Y2/T10 4002922671] DC1-2_CoolingUnit_EP1_Lvl-Sw + KF14 faulty (charging interuptions) CRM:00472000546
additional_info.body:
Dear Alexander,
After the intervention today we found that the issue with the charging curves is due the fact that the ELM system is sending 0kW profiles mix with 300KW.
In the logs, we see while charging with more than 300kW, studently we receive a new value from ELM with 0kW and 2 seconds after a profile with 396kW. This makes no sense and the ELMS must be configured to avoid sending this huge variation of values.
If I look just for the ELMS logs we can see this happening multiples times during the charging session.
From the charger point of view there is nothing wrong. We run a charging session and the curve is flat as expected.
With best regards,
Joao Francisco Louro Cardoso
Siemens S.A.
